lead: New York plumbing ranges from prewar city buildings to lake-effect snow country. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers from New York City to Buffalo.
risk: aging pipes in older buildings, frozen pipes upstate and basement flooding
risk_short: old pipes, frozen pipes and flooding
why: New York City and older upstate cities have huge numbers of prewar buildings with galvanized supply lines, cast-iron stacks and lead service lines. Steam heat, shared risers and tight access make repairs in older buildings slow.

Upstate, lake-effect snow and deep cold freeze pipes in Buffalo, Rochester and Syracuse. Heavy rain floods basements across the state. New York has no statewide plumber license; New York City licenses master plumbers, and other cities set their own rules.
tips: Insulate pipes on outside walls and in basements.
Ask your utility about your service line material.
Test your sump pump before spring thaw.
Keep grease out of shared drain stacks.
areas: Calls come from New York City, Long Island, Westchester, the Hudson Valley, the Capital Region, Syracuse, Rochester and Buffalo.

faq.q: Do plumbers need a license in New York?
faq.a: There is no statewide plumber license. New York City requires a licensed master plumber for most work, and many other cities and counties license plumbers. Check with your local building department.
